author: Sam Guzman
title: UTEP football wraps up 2026 spring season - NewsBreak
text:
By Sam Guzman ,
1 hours ago EL PASO, Texas (KTSM) — UTEP football officially closed out its 2026 spring season Wednesday morning at Glory Field, completing its 15th and final practice of the spring.
The session marked the Miners’ second workout since last Saturday’s spring game at the Sun Bowl, giving the team an opportunity to address areas of concern and build on what they saw during the scrimmage before heading into the summer months.
With all 15 practices now complete, the Miners leave spring encouraged by the progress made over the past several weeks, while also recognizing there is still work to be done ahead of the 2026 season.
“Overall, I think it was probably the most physical spring that we’ve had,” UTEP football head coach Scotty Walden said. “I think the player driven leadership has taken another step. It’s not where we need to be. Execution isn’t where it needs to be yet. The foundation that we’ve laid, we got to keep that momentum and get these guys here in the summer and build upon that.”
“I feel like as a team, we are trending in the right direction. [We are] understanding everything that the coaches want,” UTEP football redshirt sophomore quarterback EJ Colson said. “I feel like it was a great stepping point to the season. We got to take another step this summer and continue to roll that into the fall camp.”
One notable development surrounding the program comes off the field. With the NCAA eliminating the spring transfer portal window, head coach Scotty Walden and his staff have added clarity moving forward. The roster that exits spring is now largely the group UTEP will carry into the upcoming season, eliminating the uncertainty that previously followed spring practices.
With spring ball now in the rearview mirror, UTEP will shift its focus to summer training as preparations continue for the 2026 campaign.
